messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Interlingua, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Interlingua line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------|------------------|--------| | A | preposition indicating direction toward the addressees | a | to | OK | | le | definite article (plural) | — *(omitted)* | — | UNNECESSARY | | quai | relative pronoun referring to the addressees | illes | they | OK | | poi | adverb marking temporal succession (“afterwards”) | postea | thereafter | OK | | se | conditional conjunction “if” | si | if | OK | | tu | 2nd‑person singular pronoun (subject) | tu | you | OK | | vorrai | future of *volere* – “will want” | volera | will want | OK | | salire | infinitive “to ascend” | ascender | ascend | OK | | anima | noun “soul” | anima | soul | OK | | fia | future of *essere* – “shall be” | essera | shall be | OK | | a | preposition introducing the domain of worthiness (≈ “for”) | de | of/for | OK | | ciò | demonstrative pronoun “that” (referring to the ascent) | isto | that | OK | | più | comparative adverb “more” | plus | more | OK | | di | preposition introducing the standard of comparison (“than”) | que | than | OK | | me | pronoun “I” (object of comparison) | io | I | OK | | degna | adjective “worthy” | digne | worthy | OK | | con | preposition “with” | con | with | OK | | lei | pronoun “her” | illa | her | OK | | ti | pronoun “you” (accusative) | te | you | OK | | lascerò | future of *lasciare* – “will leave” | lassa | will leave | OK | | nel | contraction *in + il* – “in the/at the” | al | at the | OK | | mio | possessive adjective “my” | mi | my | OK | | partire | infinitive “to depart”, nominalised as “departure” | partite | departure | **WRONG** (should be *partita*) |
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY:** *le* – the definite article is not required before the pronoun *illes* in Interlingua. - **WRONG:** *partite* – the nominalised form of *partire* should be *partita* (singular feminine) to match the intended meaning “departure”.
All other mappings are correct and grammatically appropriate for Interlingua.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Interlingua script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Interlingua text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 1: - Original: a illes, si tu volera ascender postea, - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- Line 2: - Original: un anima essera plus digne de isto que io: - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- Line 3: - Original: con illa io lassa te al mi partite; - Issue: WRONG (the nominalised form of *partire* should be **partida**) - Corrected: con illa io lassa te al mi partida;
``` a illes, si tu volera ascender postea, un anima essera plus digne de isto que io: con illa io lassa te al mi partida; ```
